## Compiling NSD with XDP¶
As this feature is experimental and introduces new dependencies to NSD, it needs to be compiled in with `--enable-xdp`.
The additional dependencies are: `libxdp libbpf libcap clang llvm` (and `gcc-multilib` to fix a missing `asm/types.h` file, if you’re on Ubuntu).
For Debian/Ubuntu based systems, you would install the dependencies as follows:
sudo apt install -y libxdp-dev libbpf-dev libcap-dev clang llvm gcc-multilib
When using the git source repository, make sure to also initialize the submodules and auxilary files:
git clone https://github.com/NLnetLabs/nsd --branch features/af-xdp  
cd nsd  
git submodule update --init  
autoreconf -fi
After installing the dependencies, you can build NSD:
./configure --enable-xdp  
make -j4  
sudo make install

## Configuring XDP¶
The configuration options are described in nsd.conf(5).
By default, you can enable XDP for a single interface that supports it, with the `xdp-interface` option:
server:  
    xdp-interface: enp1s0
In this configuration, NSD will load and (after stopping NSD) unload its bundled XDP program that redirects UDP traffic to port 53 directly to NSD user-space. You usually don’t have to do anything else. If it doesn’t work, check out the It’s not working section.
Note
Even though NSD uses libxdp, NSD skips the xdp-dispatcher. This is done so that NSD can unload the XDP program itself when finished without requiring the SYS_ADMIN capability (see xdp-project/xdp-tools#432 and xdp-project/xdp-tools#434 on GitHub). If you use multiple XDP programs on your system, please refer to Loading the bundled XDP program yourself, until we turn this into a config option.

## Configuring XDP in special cases¶
If you have custom requirements for the use of XDP, e.g. because you want to integrate NSD into you existing XDP setup, you have two options:
1.   Loading the bundled XDP program yourself, or

2.   Writing/Extending your own custom XDP program.

## Configuring XDP in special cases¶
### Loading the bundled XDP program yourself¶
NSD includes two XDP programs (in `/usr/share/nsd/`, by default). You’ll need the file named `xdp-dns-redirect_kern_pinned.o`. The two programs are functionally identical, the `_pinned` variant just defines the pinning option for the `xsks_map`.
When loading the program, make sure to instruct your xdp program loader of choice to pin the map and adjust the file permissions so that NSD can modify the pinned map. For example with the `xdp-loader` from xdp-tools:
sudo xdp-loader load -p /sys/fs/bpf <iface> /usr/share/nsd/xdp-dns-redirect_kern_pinned.o  
sudo chown nsd /sys/fs/bpf/xsks_map  
sudo chmod o+x /sys/fs/bpf
You’ll need to instruct NSD to not load any XDP programs, and inform NSD about which XDP program you loaded and the bpffs path used, if that differs from the default of `/sys/fs/bpf`. For example:
server:  
    xdp-interface: enp1s0
xdp-program-load: no  
    xdp-program-path: "/usr/share/nsd/xdp-dns-redirect_kern_pinned.o"  
    xdp-bpffs-path: "/sys/fs/bpf"
